Critical Feature
# Critical Feature
MCP server exposes a curated public tool surface over stdio transport

The kibi-mcp server exposes a JSON-RPC 2.0 interface over stdin/stdout.

The public MCP surface remains intentionally curated and deterministic. It includes exact retrieval (`kb_query`), discovery/reporting (`kb_search`, `kb_status`, `kb_find_gaps`, `kb_coverage`, `kb_graph`), mutation (`kb_upsert`, `kb_delete`), and validation (`kb_check`).

Read-only operations used by non-interactive clients must publish truthful MCP annotations. In particular, `kb_status` advertises read-only, non-destructive, idempotent, closed-world behavior so clients can inspect branch state without a mutation-approva
CLI with init, sync, query, check, gc, doctor commands

The `kibi` CLI provides: `init` (scaffold .kb/), `sync` (import entities from files),
`query` (filter and format KB output), `check` (run validation rules),
`gc` (remove stale branch stores), `doctor` (diagnose KB health).
'Eight entity types: req, scenario, test, adr, flag, event, symbol, fact'

The KB schema supports exactly eight typed entities. Every entity record requires the fields id, type, title, status, created_at, updated_at and source. Entity records also accept the fields priority, tags, owner and links.

## Context

The entity model is the base every Kibi feature reads and writes. The required-field list was corrected to match the entity schema, which also requires source (sync derives it from the file path), so that the claim can be proved against the schema itself.
Typed relationships between entities with audit metadata

Relationships are first-class: `implements`, `validates`, `specified_by`,
`covered_by`, `depends_on`, `relates_to`, `constrained_by`, etc.
Each relationship triple is stored in RDF with a provenance timestamp.
Built-in consistency validation rules (must-priority-coverage, no-cycles,

`kibi check` runs three built-in Prolog rules:
- `must-priority-coverage`: every `must`-priority req must have a scenario and a test
- `no-dangling-refs`: every relationship target must exist in the KB
- `no-cycles`: no circular dependency chains
Markdown and YAML manifest extractors for entity import

`kibi sync` reads entity data from:
- YAML frontmatter in Markdown files (requirements, scenarios, tests, ADRs, flags, events)
- `symbols.yaml` manifest for code symbol entries
- plain string Markdown `links` entries, imported as generic `relates_to` edges
- typed Markdown `links` objects, imported with their explicit relationship type
Git hooks for automated KB sync on branch checkout and merge

`kibi init` installs `post-checkout` and `post-merge` git hooks by default. They
keep the KB in sync with the working tree. On branch checkout, if the branch KB does not exist, it is created by copying from the resolved default branch (see brief.md for precedence: config `defaultBranch`, then `origin/HEAD`, then `main`).
RDF persistence using SWI-Prolog rdf_persistency library

The KB is stored as RDF triples using `library(semweb/rdf_persistency)`.
The on-disk format is RDF/XML at `.kb/branches/<branch>/kb.rdf`.
Prolog predicates provide the read/write interface; the CLI and MCP translate to/from JSON.
VS Code extension with TreeView sidebar for KB navigation

The VS Code extension contributes a sidebar panel with a tree view of all KB
entities grouped by type. Entities with a known source file can be opened in the
editor by clicking.
'Write governance: validated changesets and append-only audit log'

All KB writes go through `kb_upsert/2` which validates the changeset schema before
committing. The RDF store is append-only; history is preserved via `rdf_persistency`.
Copy-from-default-branch semantics for new branch KB creation

When a new branch is checked out and no KB store exists for it yet, kibi
automatically copies the resolved default branch store as the starting snapshot.
The default branch is determined in this order: (1) `.kb/config.json` `defaultBranch` if set, (2) `origin/HEAD` if available, (3) falls back to `main` only if neither is set.
This preserves continuity without requiring manual re-sync.
Deterministic inference remains available outside the public MCP tool surface

Kibi must keep deterministic inference capabilities available for product and
automation use, but they are not exposed as a raw public inference surface.

The public MCP interface remains curated: exact lookup, curated discovery/reporting,
mutation, and validation are allowed, while arbitrary inference predicates remain
internal.
Pre-commit and CI enforcement of KB consistency
`kibi init` installs a pre-commit git hook by default. The hook runs `kibi check` and blocks commits when must-priority coverage rules are violated. CI also runs `kibi check` as a real gate.
Query KB entities by source file path

The CLI and MCP server must accept a source file path as a query parameter and return
all KB entities whose source field matches that path. Public MCP access uses
`kb_query` with the `sourceFile` filter.
Temporal ADR supersession chain

The KB must support a supersedes(adr, adr) relationship type so the full chain of architectural decisions is machine-readable. Inference rules expose current_adr/1, adr_chain/2, and superseded_by/2. kibi check flags superseded/deprecated ADRs with no successor.

This enables agents to query the complete history of architectural decisions for any topic, understanding how decisions have evolved over time and which ADR is currently in effect.
Users have a maximum of 2 roles

Deprecated business rule kept as the superseded predecessor to REQ-019. 
This requirement models a strict domain constraint using the two-lane fact model.
It constrains the `FACT-USER-ROLE` subject fact and requires the `FACT-LIMIT-2` property-value fact.
This enables Kibi to programmatically detect contradictions if another requirement attempts to impose a conflicting constraint on the same subject.
Users can now have 3 roles (retired demo)

Current business rule and canonical append-only successor to REQ-018.
This requirement demonstrates how to evolve strict domain constraints. 
By using `supersedes`, Kibi understands that this requirement replaces the semantics of REQ-018, 
allowing the new constraint (maximum of 3 roles) to take precedence while maintaining a clear audit trail.

# Requirement: Release Automation with Changesets

All Kibi npm releases (core, CLI, MCP server, OpenCode plugin) must be automated using the [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) workflow. This ensures:

- Consistent semantic versioning across all npm packages
- Automated changelog generation
- Safe, auditable, and reproducible releases
- Integration with CI/CD for publish gates and release verification

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Automation**: All release steps are automated via Changesets.
- **Versioning on Develop**: Version bumps and changelog updates happen on `develop`

Agent-guided migration orchestration

Kibi exposes a single typed migration plan so agents can inspect deterministic
repair work and distinguish it from semantic, operator, and execution work.
Status and checks are read-only; only explicitly approved automatic actions may
be applied, and every application is followed by a fresh readback.
Codex, Cursor and ZCode hooks guard firm rules and capture stated decisions

Before an edit changes code that implements a current firm requirement, the Codex, Cursor, ZCode pre-edit hooks must tell the agent to ask the person before an edit that breaks that rule, once per requirement per session. When a submitted prompt reads as a rule, the Codex, Cursor, ZCode hooks must give the agent the note that recording the rule with kb_upsert is part of the change. When a session that changed source files stops without any kb_upsert write, the Codex, Cursor, ZCode stop hooks must ask the agent once per session to record the decision behind the change.
